newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi does not rule out modest mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi does not rule out modest mini-budget.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday he could not rule out a "modest" mini-budget and said he would still like to bring forward the full 1998 budget but would need clear backing in parliament to do so.
Prodi told a news conference after a cabinet meeting that he did not exclude a mini-budget for this year of "modest size".
"We don't exclude a corrective mini-budget of not too large size, modest, and within a few weeks we will make the decsion about this corrective action," he said.
The government has been mulling whether to draft a deficit cutting mini-budget and whether to begin debating next year's budget early.
Prodi and his economic ministers say both would send a strong signal of Italian stability ahead of European Economic and Monetary Union.
Opposition centre-right bloc leader Silvio Berlusconi has offered to work with the coalition on an early 1998 budget in return for a combined assault on welfare reform.
The government is targeting a 1997 deficit of 61.4 trillion lire ($36.8 billion) after 138.5 trillion last year, well above forecast.
Prodi has already said that any mini-budget to compensate for the overshoot would cut spending -- putting the government on a potential collision course with Communist Refoundation.
His coalition depends on the hard-left party for its majority in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house).

Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni has said the government would wait for official state accounts, which are due out by early March, before making up its mind on a mini-budget. -- Rome newsroom +396-678-505 ($ = 1666 Italian Lire)
